Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: bcm283x: Use firmware PM driver for V3D

The register based driver turned out to be unstable, specially on RPi3a+
but not limited to it. While a fix is being worked on, we roll back to
using firmware based scheme.

Fixes: e1dc2b2e1bef ("ARM: bcm283x: Switch V3D over to using the PM driver instead of firmware")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Saenz Julienne <nsaenzjulienne@suse.de>
Tested-by: Stefan Wahren <stefan.wahren@i2se.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200303173217.3987-1-nsaenzjulienne@suse.de

Here is the root cause:
The instability of the register-based driver for the V3D GPU, particularly on the Raspberry Pi 3a+, led to the decision to revert to a firmware-based power management scheme. This indicates that the register-based implementation was likely not handling power management correctly, causing crashes or erratic behavior in the GPU.

Here is the patch:
 			reg = <0x7ec00000 0x1000>;
 			interrupts = <1 10>;
-			power-domains = <&pm BCM2835_POWER_DOMAIN_GRAFX_V3D>;
 		};

Reason:
This line indicates that the register-based driver was attempting to manage the power domain for the V3D GPU using the PM driver, which turned out to be unstable, particularly on the Raspberry Pi 3a+. The instability likely stemmed from improper handling of power management, leading to crashes or erratic behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-			power-domains = <&pm BCM2835_POWER_DOMAIN_GRAFX_V3D>;
```
Reason:
By removing the line that specifies the power domain for the V3D GPU, the system reverts to using the firmware-based power management scheme. This change eliminates the instability associated with the register-based driver, allowing for more reliable operation of the GPU, especially on affected hardware like the Raspberry Pi 3a+.
